newsitem.title: USA: Damp weather impedes Missouri crop harvests.
newsitem.headline: Damp weather impedes Missouri crop harvests.

text.p: Cool, damp weather slowed harvesting of Missouri's cotton, sorghum and soybeans during the week ended Sunday, according to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
Soybeans were 86 percent harvested versus 98 a year ago and the 93 percent average. Harvest in the southeast lagged the most at 65 percent complete.
Corn was 89 percent harvested versus 92 a year ago and the 89 average. The northern areas were least advanced, ranging from 82 to 85 percent.
Sorghum was 88 percent harvested versus 92 a year ago and the 91 average.
Cotton was 80 percent harvested, virtually unchanged from a week ago. This compares with 95 percent a year ago and the 93 average.

Winter wheat was 91 percent seeded, versus 99 a year ago and the five-year average of 92. The crop was 79 percent emerged versus 84 a year ago and the 79 average. It was rated four percent excellent, 56 good, 36 fair and four poor.
Topsoil moisture was rated 35 percent surplus, 63 adequate, and two short. Pasture and range rated five percent excellent, 49 poor, 36 fair, nine poor and one very poor.
